record.original_question: Does the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, in which weak turbulence transfers energy to high frequencies and triggers black-hole formation, persist or change qualitatively once one goes beyond the spherically symmetric scalar-field model to more general perturbations and matter models?

evidence.quote: Problem P8: Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability in Anti￰de Sitter spacetime, which leads to a weakly turbulent mechanism that develops a cascade towards high frequencies leading to black hole formation, behaves dif￰ferently in more general models than spherically symmetric scalar field collapse.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of (d+1)-dimensional Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, i.e. the maximally symmetric Lorentzian solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations with negative cosmological constant Λ < 0. With reflecting boundary conditions imposed at conformal infinity, AdS behaves as a confining cavity in which finite-energy perturbations cannot disperse to infinity.

It has been conjectured that AdS is nonlinearly unstable: arbitrarily small generic perturbations evolve so that energy is transferred via a weakly turbulent cascade from low to arbitrarily high frequency modes, eventually producing a trapped surface and hence a black hole. This conjecture is strongly supported in the spherically symmetric model of Einstein gravity coupled to a real massless scalar field.

Question. Determine whether this conjectured nonlinear instability of AdS — together with its weakly turbulent high-frequency cascade and black-hole formation mechanism — persists, qualitatively changes, or fails when one moves beyond the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field setting to:
(i) purely gravitational (non-spherically symmetric) perturbations of AdS governed by the vacuum Einstein equations with Λ < 0;
(ii) perturbations breaking both spherical and axial symmetry;
(iii) AdS coupled to other matter models (e.g. perfect fluids, gauge fields, complex scalars, etc.).

In particular, characterize which classes of small initial data on AdS lead to black-hole formation in finite time and which lead to globally regular, possibly quasi-periodic, solutions, and identify the structural features (resonances, normal-mode spectrum, symmetry assumptions) responsible for any qualitative differences from the spherically symmetric scalar case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open in general. Numerical and perturbative work beyond spherical symmetry (Dias–Horowitz–Santos and follow-ups, 2016–2017) shows that the gravitational sector behaves qualitatively differently from the spherical scalar case: many normal modes cannot be extended to periodic horizonless solutions, and resonance structures differ. Recent work (2025) on slowly rotating Kerr-AdS provides further nonlinear instability results without symmetry, but a complete characterization of AdS nonlinear (in)stability for general perturbations and matter models has not been established.

status_evidence.title: AdS nonlinear instability: moving beyond spherical symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Gravitational sector behaves differently; not all gravitational normal modes extend to periodic horizonless solutions; single-mode seeds can develop secular resonances unlike the spherical scalar case.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond spherical symmetry, the instability mechanism differs qualitatively but is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: AdS nonlinear instability: breaking spherical and axial symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Little is known about nonlinear instability in the purely gravitational sector where spherical symmetry is necessarily broken; single gravitational normal mode rarely backreacts to a nonlinear solution.
status_evidence.claim: The fully gravitational, non-symmetric problem remains largely open.

status_evidence.title: Non-linear instability of slowly rotating Kerr-AdS black holes
status_evidence.snippet: Stable trapping of generic perturbations of Kerr-AdS persists at the non-linear level; spacetime settles into a time-dependent non-axisymmetric black hole.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work extends nonlinear instability results to rotating AdS settings without symmetry assumptions.
